subject: maths
title: Repeating Patterns
seo_title: Year 1 Repeating Patterns Worksheets: Shapes, Colours and Numbers (Free, Australian Curriculum)
standard_text: Recognise, continue and create repeating patterns with numbers, symbols, shapes and objects, identifying the repeating unit
meta_desc: Free Year 1 maths worksheets on repeating patterns: continue AB, ABB, AAB and ABC patterns, find the repeating unit, fill in the missing part, and make patterns with shapes, colours, objects, numbers and symbols. 100 picture questions with an answer key, following the Australian Curriculum.
key_big: Find the part that repeats. Then say it again and again.
key_sub: That part is the repeating unit. Finish each unit before you start it again, and check the whole unit repeats in the same order.
body_html:
What is a repeating pattern?

A repeating pattern has a part that comes again and again. That part is called the repeating unit. Find the unit. Then say it again and again to keep the pattern going.

PatternRepeating unitThings in the unit
red, blue, red, bluered, blue2
circle, star, star, circle, star, starcircle, star, star3
1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 31, 2, 33
clap, clap, stamp, stamp, clap, clap, stamp, stampclap, clap, stamp, stamp4

What comes next?

Find where the last unit stops. Then keep saying the unit.

Example

What comes next? 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, 1, ?

The repeating unit is 1, 2, 3. The last unit so far is 1. Next is 2. This pattern repeats. It does not count on.

Answer: 2

What is missing?

Start at the beginning. Say the unit along the row, one thing at a time. When you reach the gap, the word you say is the answer.

Example

Red, red, blue, red, ?, blue. What is missing?

The repeating unit is red, red, blue. Say it: red, red, blue, red, red, blue.

Answer: red

Make a pattern

Choose a unit, such as yellow, blue. Make it again and again: yellow, blue, yellow, blue. A row is only a repeating pattern if the same unit repeats every time, in the same order.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Starting the unit again too early: red, blue, blue, red, blue, redFinish the unit first: red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue
Unit too short: calling red, blue, blue a red, blue patternLook for where the whole unit starts again
Copying the thing just before the gapSay the unit from the start of the row
Counting on: 1, 2, 3, 1, 2, 3, then 4In a repeating pattern, 1, 2, 3 comes back again

faq.q: What is a repeating unit in Year 1 maths?
faq.a: The repeating unit is the part of a pattern that repeats again and again. In red, blue, blue, red, blue, blue, the repeating unit is red, blue, blue. Year 1 students identify the repeating unit to continue and create patterns (AC9M1A02).

faq.q: What kinds of repeating patterns do Year 1 students learn?
faq.a: They work with patterns of colours, shapes, objects, numbers and symbols, such as AB (red, blue), ABB (circle, star, star), AAB and ABC patterns. They continue a pattern, find a missing part and make their own.

faq.q: How can I help my child with patterns at home?
faq.a: Make patterns with beads, blocks, pegs or leaves, or with actions such as clap, stamp, stamp. Ask your child to say the pattern aloud, point to the repeating unit and tell you what comes next.

faq.q: Why are repeating patterns part of algebra?
faq.a: Finding a repeating unit means noticing a rule and using it to predict what comes next. This is the start of algebraic thinking in the Australian Curriculum, and it leads to skip counting and number patterns.
